newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada urges democracy in Congo, Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Canada urges democracy in Congo, Sierra Leone.

text.p: Canada on Tuesday called for democracy in the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, and in Sierra Leone.

Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy called on Laurent Kabila, the self-proclaimed president of Congo, to form a broad-based government, undertake reconstruction of the country and help humanitarian agencies dealing with refugees.

"This change of orientation requires the establishment of the rule of law and democratic institutions, good governance practices and a transparent electoral process that would lead to free and fair legislative and presidential elections at the earliest possible date," Axworthy said in a statement.

Canada had cool relations with Zaire under the regime of former President Mobuto Sese Seko, but Axworthy said Ottawa would reconsider its ties with the Democratic Republic of Congo, depending on the steps taken by Kabila to restore democracy.
Kabila's forces marched into Kinshasa on May 17, effectively ousting Mobutu.

On Tuesday, South African President Nelson Mandela accused Western governments of demonizing Kabila and said a ban on political activity imposed by the former rebel leader was understandable under the circumstances.
Canada also condemned last weekend's coup in Sierra Leone as "unacceptable" and called for speedy restoration of constitutional order.
"It is all the more tragic after Sierra Leone's real progress toward democracy, peace and economic reconstruction since early last year," said Axworthy.
Canada has urged the Commonwealth countries to consider the Sierra Leone coup at its meeting in early July and make recommendations.

Sierra Leone's ousted president, Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, said on Tuesday he wanted West African states to restore his government to power and sanctions to be imposed against army corporals who engineered the coup, the third military takeover in Sierra Leone in five years.
